queer_characters.name: Melville Farr
queer_characters.notes: Described as a closeted gay barrister with a romantic past with Barrett; the film is noted as the first British film to explicitly name homosexuality and treat it sympathetically. Portrayed as courageous, sacrificing his career to expose blackmailers targeting gay men.

queer_characters.name: Jack Barrett
queer_characters.notes: Young man with a romantic past with Farr; compromised by blackmailers and dies by suicide in custody, reflecting the persecution of gay men under criminalization.

contributor_notes: Landmark 1961 British film credited with liberalizing attitudes toward homosexuality; given an 'X' rating on release. Barrett's suicide could arguably support a 'bury-your-gays' tag, but given the historical context and sympathetic framing I've marked only tragic-queer — a maintainer may wish to reconsider.
